text:
Oncall-Bot: ALERT: node flapping detected in inference-pool-us-west-2. 3 NotReady events in 4m. Auto-escalating to on-call. Incident ID INC-1765432100
Kai: I'm on it. seeing kubelet restarts on node i-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7. pinging infra.
Marie: Noticed higher 5xx from the hosted API around the same time, ~30s spikes every minute. Possible pod reschedules.
AJ: Can you paste the node status? I can run quick checks.
Kai: kubectl get nodes --selector=pool=inference -o wide

```
NAME                              STATUS     ROLES    AGE   VERSION
ip-10-0-12-34.us-west-2.compute   NotReady   <none>   42d   v1.25.8
ip-10-0-56-78.us-west-2.compute   Ready      <none>   42d   v1.25.8
ip-10-0-23-45.us-west-2.compute   NotReady   <none>   42d   v1.25.8
```

Kai: kubelet logs show repeated `kubelet: panic` and then systemd restarts.
Sara: Any GPU driver OOMs? Could be CUDA crashing and bringing kubelet into bad state.
AJ: Checking dmesg from one affected node:

```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 1234.568000] kernel: GPU reset detected
```

AJ: yep, GPU resets. That usually causes inference containers to crash and node kubelet to get into churn on our config.
Marie: Customer impact? Which customers routed to that pool?
Kai: We route prod-large models and some enterprise customers; routing policy was region-preferred so affected customers in us-west-2.
Sara: Init mitigation: cordon the two NotReady nodes? They are already NotReady.
AJ: To stop further cascading, I'm going to scale down the inference DaemonSet on non-ready nodes and reroute new traffic to healthy pool.
DeployBot: Rollout request: route-policy update -> route customers in us-west-2 from inference-pool to inference-pool-fallback. Initiated.
Kai: Manual steps I'm doing: 1) drain any surviving pods on flapping nodes 2) annotate node for GPU-evac-check 3) open ticket to infra for hardware investigation.

```
kubectl drain ip-10-0-12-34 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
kubectl annotate node ip-10-0-12-34 inference.redwood/evac-check=true
```

Sara: I'll open a PagerDuty incident for infra/hardware to check the NIC/GPU firmware. PD#PD-1245
AJ: Also enabling temporary autoscale on dedicated pool to absorb load: scaled target replicas from 120 -> 160.
Marie: Monitoring: dashboards show 5xx error rate dropped from 12% -> 1.6% after route-policy change and scaling. Latency normalized.
Kai: Customer comms: We should notify affected enterprise tenants with a short note. Who owns that? Marie?
Marie: I'll draft a quick status: "We experienced a regional GPU driver instability causing node restarts in the us-west-2 inference pool. Traffic was routed to fallback, impact mitigated. We're investigating hardware and driver versions." Will post to #customer-status.
Sara: Any idea root cause? recent driver rollout or kernel update?
AJ: I see a node with NV driver 535.86; one healthy node has 535.54. There was a planned infra node image update yesterday.
Kai: Noted. Put a hold on infra image rollouts for this cluster. ops-sre, can you halt the staged rollout? @ops-sre
ops-sre: Received. Pausing image rollout for us-west-2 and opening a rollback task.
DeployBot: Route-policy revert disabled. Fallback remains active until further notice.
Marie: I'll follow up with affected customers after we have a driver rollback plan. For now, incident severity -> SEV2 (regional impact degraded but service available via fallback).
Kai: Handoff: I'm on for another 30m then will pass to AJ for monitoring and infra ticket follow-up. AJ, can you take the next shift on this one?
AJ: Yep taking over. I'll keep the PD incident open and update infra ticket with GPU logs + node serials. Will post final update when driver rollback complete or hardware confirmed.
Oncall-Bot: Note: Next rotation @ 1765432300. Incident thread pinned. Reactions: :rotating_light: :hammer_and_wrench:
Sara: After-action items: (1) add GPU driver compatibility test in canary (2) add kubelet health-check that isolates node earlier (3) improve autoscale buffer for regional pools.
Marie: Agreed. I'll create tickets and link to this thread.
AJ: Closing loop: current metrics stable; no further NotReady events in the last 6m. Leaving PD open until infra ack. 
Kai: Thanks team. Good mitigation; leaving cordon/annotation for infra to validate before uncordon.
